meta.extension: ext-rabbit_rs 0.2.2 — release cdylib (target/release/librabbit_rs_php.dylib), loaded per-run via -d extension=..., never installed system-wide
meta.broker: RabbitMQ 4.2.9 — local 3-node lab cluster + toxiproxy (./scripts/lab-up.sh with-plugin, ./scripts/lab-ready.sh verified)
meta.protocol: ./scripts/rebench-driver-bench.sh — 3 interleaved passes over 5 cells, count=1000, rounds=10 (10,000 measured ops per cell per pass), ~1024 B Laravel queue envelope, quorum queue, prefetch 64

reference_other_drivers.note: Measured in the same interleaved session for context only. NOT budget-checked: third-party drivers shift for external reasons (their own releases, their broker-side behavior), and a shift there is not a rabbit-rs regression.

notes: All numbers are real runs of ./scripts/rebench-driver-bench.sh on this machine (Apple M2 Max, macOS 26.6.2, Docker 29.2.1, RabbitMQ 4.2.9 lab), release cdylib, interleaved passes per the release protocol.

Baseline values are the median of the 3 recorded runs per cell. Raw per-run values are kept above for provenance; the run JSONs themselves live under benchmarks/results/ws8-baseline-runs/ (gitignored) — copy them out before wiping results/.

Observed run-to-run variance: transient mid-run dips of 30-55% hit 2 of 3 rabbit-rs cells once each (goopil-dispatch-safe run2 round 1, goopil-worker run2 rounds 5-7); clean runs sit within ~±10% of the median. This is why the checker compares the median of an invocation's runs per scenario, not each file separately, and why the throughput floor is 80% of the median.

Measurement tree state: d3e7a4e. Two later commits (7792b0e auto_subscribe compile-time rejection, 58d32b0 docs) postdate the runs; neither touches the measured path. Pre-fix truth: the archived run JSONs record auto_subscribe=true — at d3e7a4e the compiler accepted and propagated the key (the compile-time rejection only landed in 7792b0e), but it never took effect on the measured path: the compiler already derived a worker profile covering the bench queue, so pop() resolved it without ever reaching the auto_subscribe fallback. Post-fix the key is rejected at compile time and removed from the bench connection, and the compiled shape pins auto_subscribe=false.

Soak-schema evidence (benchmarks/results/round-k-soak) carries no throughput/latency metrics and is not part of this baseline; the checker still applies its always-blocking integrity checks to such files.
